pr_title: Don't double type-bound CHECK constraints in create_table
pr_body:
Fixed issue where, when using SQLAlchemy 2.1, the CHECK constraint
generated by a type such as Enum or Boolean with
create_constraint=True would be rendered by autogenerate as explicit
sa.CheckConstraint() entries within op.create_table(), in addition to
the type itself which already produces that constraint, leading to a
duplicate constraint error when the migration is run.

Fixed issue where a CreateTableOp produced from an existing Table
using CreateTableOp.from_table() would emit the CHECK constraint
generated by a type such as Enum or Boolean with
create_constraint=True twice in the resulting CREATE TABLE statement
when invoked directly.

Fixes: #1884
Change-Id: I851bee2daf3bcc9eb437a1b42692b42974cddf46
plant_patch:
diff --git a/alembic/operations/schemaobj.py b/alembic/operations/schemaobj.py
index 6ebecf8d..a8d11b9a 100644
--- a/alembic/operations/schemaobj.py
+++ b/alembic/operations/schemaobj.py
@@ -233,7 +233,7 @@ class SchemaObjects:
                 # by the column's type when the column was added to the
                 # Table above, so skip it here so that it isn't doubled.
                 # SQLAlchemy to_metadata() skips these in the same way
-                and not sqla_compat._is_type_bound(elem)
+                and sqla_compat._is_type_bound(elem)
             )
         ]
